articles.title: Kojima’s Physint Dropped By PlayStation, Rescued By Xbox
articles.summary: Sony has revealed today that it will no longer be working with Kojima Productions on stealth action game Physint, while Kojima announced that Xbox has stepped up to rescue the project.
body: PlayStation's official statement didn't say why it chose to end its support of Physint, leaving gamers to speculate on the reasons behind its shock exit. "We continue to have great admiration for Hideo Kojima's vision for the game," Sony said, adding, "we look forward to continued close collaboration with Hideo Kojima and his award-winning independent studio in the future."

Kojima posted from his personal account with more details, saying that PlayStation cancelled Physint as of mid-June this year, and the new collaboration with Xbox came as a result of the studio's determination to keep the project alive.

"We're honored that Kojima-san has chosen Xbox to work with Kojima Productions on Physint," said Xbox CEO Asha Sharma in a statement. "His ambition to challenge conventions reflects the kind of creativity we want to support at Xbox."

Though it may be surprising after Kojima's long history of collaborating with PlayStation, from his work at Konami to both Death Stranding games, Kojima also has an existing working relationship with Xbox, which is publishing his upcoming horror game OD.
points: Sony has revealed today that it will no longer be working with Kojima Productions on stealth action game Physint, while Kojima announced that Xbox has stepped up to rescue the project.

articles.title: Proof-of-Age Verification for Steam in Australia Now Only Possible Using a Credit Card
articles.summary: Valve has implemented a proof-of-age verification system for Australian Steam users, which was required due to new laws in the country forcing online gaming platforms to require users to prove they are over 18 years of age to access games classified R18+.
body: However, unlike PlayStation and Xbox (which offer multiple ways to verify you’re over 18), Valve has opted that it will only accept ownership of an actual credit card as sufficient proof of age. Despite some users anecdotally reporting otherwise, it does not appear debit cards are sufficient, and nor is PayPal. It also doesn’t matter if your Steam account is already well over 20 years old.

“Valve is required by the Age-Restricted Material App Distribution Services Code to verify that you are 18 or older before accessing mature content. If you wish to do so, please add a valid Australian credit card to your account and afterwards update the Mature Content Preferences.”

Of course, not all Australian Steam users over 18 have a credit card, or indeed want a credit card – when there are already a ton of more convenient ways to make purchases online. Unfortunately for Australian Steam users, an active credit card is all Valve is willing to accept, despite other methods of verification being readily available. This active credit card also reportedly needs to remain active on the account, even if you do not want to make purchases with it.

articles.title: Hideo Kojima's Metal Gear Solid Spiritual Successor Physint Will Now Be Published by Xbox Instead of Sony
articles.summary: Renowned video game director Hideo Kojima's upcoming project Physint, which could fairly be described as a spiritual successor to Metal Gear Solid, will now be published by Xbox instead of Sony, Microsoft announced today.
body: Xbox will continue to publish Kojima's horror game OD — itself something of a spiritual successor to the never-finished PT — and the Kojima-Xbox partnership will expand beyond these two game projects to include film and television.

“This expands our relationship with Xbox beyond OD. As we move forward with the development of Physint, we remain committed to redefining the action-espionage genre for players around the world,” Kojima said.

Xbox CEO Asha Sharma, who took over from the retiring Phil Spencer earlier this year, made Kojima a priority in her quest to reset and rebuild Xbox, including the return of console exclusives that begins with Gears of War: E-Day this year and continues with Clockwork Revolution in 2027. In terms of Kojima Productions projects, OD will be released before Physint. In July, IGN reported that OD was safe from Sharma's big "reset" of the Xbox business, which has seen thousands of staff lose their jobs, multiple studios go independent, and various video game projects canceled.
points: Renowned video game director Hideo Kojima's upcoming project Physint, which could fairly be described as a spiritual successor to Metal Gear Solid, will now be published by Xbox instead of Sony…

articles.title: The 10 Most Anticipated Board Games of Fall 2026
articles.summary: After spending summer traveling or enjoying the nice weather outside, fall’s plunging temperatures offer the perfect excuse to stay indoors and play some games. But beyond a packed release schedule for video games, fall is a huge time for board games, with many new titles previewing and releasing…
body: Even if you can’t make it to the world’s largest board game fair, there are highly successful crowdfunded games finally getting their retail release, and a tie-in to Dune: Part Three to look forward to. Whether you want something casual to play with the family or a deeply complex game that will take all day to complete, these are the 10 most anticipated board games releasing this fall, ordered by estimated release date.

The designers of the epic dark fantasy game Oathsworn return with an Arthurian area control game that raised $2 million on Gamefound. Two to four players control asymmetric factions exploring the isle of Avalon, searching for artifacts and mythical beasts. You can recruit powerful allies to join your cause, build settlements, hunt for the holy grail, and try to complete prophecies that could make you the next wielder of Excalibur. The art and miniatures are impressively detailed and serious fans can splurge on upgraded components or a fey-focused expansion.

articles.summary: The first glimpses of DC Studios’ The People v. Gorilla Grodd indicates it’s shaping up to be just as wacky as a TV show about a talking genius gorilla hailing from the creators of American Vandal could possibly get. The People v.
body: The People v. Gorilla Grodd is an eight-part true crime documentary series hosted by The Daily Planet’s Jimmy Olsen (once again played by Superman’s Skyler Gisondo ), who is investigating whether Grodd was wrongly imprisoned for killing his father, King Grodd.
Jimmy Tatro has been cast as Gorilla Grodd, but the actor recently explained that his role is mostly voice work and that motion-capture will be used to record his facial expressions.

That would explain why there’s a performer in a gorilla costume in the set photos and videos all over social media while the production films at Georgia Institute of Technology. It’s likely the suit performer is a stand-in for what will eventually become a CGI character.

The set photos and videos show Grodd attending Metropolis University, graduating in his cap and gown, singing with an a cappella group, and serenading a young woman with the Backstreet Boys’ "As Long as You Love Me". articles.title: The Practical Acer 16" 1080p Portable USB Monitor Is on Sale For Just $39.99 at Best Buy
articles.summary: It's no surprise why USB portable monitors are so popular. They provide extra screen real estate for laptop users and they're much slimmer and lighter than your average monitor so you can carry them around.
body: Best Buy currently has the lowest price on a brand-name portable monitor. For a limited time, you can pick up a certified refurbished Acer 15.6" USB Portable Monitor (PM161Q) for just $39.99 with free shipping. It comes with a 90-day warranty.

The Acer PM161Q is a portable 15.6" monitor that weighs in at just 1.5 pounds and measures about 0.41" thin. It's small and slim enough to fit inside a laptop bag or backpack. It sports a sturdy metal frame and includes a cover that doubles as a kickstand. The 15.6" IPS display features a 1080p resolution (141ppi), 60Hz refresh rate, wide 178-degree viewing angle, and an anti-glare matte surface. It even has a built-in speaker.

Connectivity options include two USB Type-C ports and one mini HDMI port to connect to a laptop, tablet, or handheld gaming PC for use as a main or secondary display. If your device is equipped with a USB Type-C output with Power Delivery, then a single cable can be used for both video and power. Otherwise, you'll need two cables: a mini HDMI or USB Type-C cable for video and a second USB Type-C cable to a wall charger for power. All necessary cables are included.

articles.title: Investor Accidentally Pitches Kickass Pokemon Apocalypse Movie
articles.summary: For more than three decades, Pokemon and its various card and video games have enjoyed sustained popularity around the world. And at least one prominent collector and investor--Griffin Gaming Partners co-founder Peter Levin--believes that Pokemon's enduring appeal not only extends to the present…
body: "Pokemon is a global phenomenon," Levin told The Hollywood Reporter. "I'm absolutely convinced that if the world suffered an apocalypse tomorrow, the following day the global currency would be Pokemon cards. Pokemon cards are beating the S&P 500 by 3,000%. Emanating from Japan, it really took hold around the world in the late '90s and early 2000s. It then had a zenith moment and then a nadir moment, and ever since then, it's been on a parabolic growth curve."

As unlikely as that scenario might seem, there could be a very entertaining movie based on survivors using Pokemon cards as currency during an apocalypse. It would be probably even better with actual Pokemon--like the Detective Pikachu movie--but Levin's really hit on fun idea even if it doesn't have a basis in reality.

Everything Levin said about Pokemon's popularity is correct. There's a reason why the Japanese mob reportedly used rare Pokemon cards to launder money or for increasingly brazen robberies of Pokemon cards from stores across the US. Some people are willing to pay ridiculous amounts of money for the rarest Pokemon cards and collectibles.

articles.title: 31 Years Later, Matthew Lillard’s Fan-Favorite Techno-Thriller Is Officially Free on Streaming
articles.summary: Which brings us to the 1995 cyber-thriller Hackers, a film that feels specifically designed to produce maximum Matthew Lillard energy. Directed by Iain Softley, the film follows a group of teenage punks with a knack for hacking, who get caught in a corporate embezzlement scheme after one of their…
body: Matthew Lillard has always been the perfect actor to amplify the fun in any film. Whether he's a horror-movie killer or an energetic stoner, Lillard has a special ability to make even the strangest characters unforgettable. His breakout came with Serial Mom and Scream, before he became permanently associated with Shaggy in both Scooby-Doo and Scooby-Doo 2: Monsters Unleashed. More recently, he's found another generation of fans through projects like Five Nights at Freddy's and Daredevil. There is something wonderful about how his commitment never wavers, even when the material gets completely ridiculous.

Lillard plays Emmanuel Goldstein, aka Cereal Killer, a member of the primary hacker crew that also includes Dade Murphy (Jonny Lee Miller) and Kate Libby (Angelina Jolie). Goldstein is the group's resident burnout, conspiracy theorist, and walking collection of '90s slang. Early on, he takes a seat in an English class he isn't enrolled in, offhandedly asking if he’s in the wrong room only when caught. It’s a throwaway moment that reveals he’s not only irreverent but convinced he's the coolest guy in the room.

body: Both of these shows amassed widespread acclaim for how they tackle their subject matter. Each series focuses on murder investigations told through a female lens. The underlying premise was the same, but approached differently, which made the stories unique.
For fans of crime, and for fans of Mare of Easttown and Killing Eve, this show captures all the elements that hooked viewers.

Hulu's Furious is not an easy watch at times, but it is one that feels entirely necessary. The subjects it focuses on are never sugarcoated or pushed to the side. The show follows FBI agent Alice Black (Emmy Rossum) as she investigates Catherine Grace (Lola Petticrew), a female serial killer targeting a web of abusive, predatory men. Grace herself was a victim of these men, who sex-trafficked her when she was young.

articles.title: A Full-Fledged Skyrim Mod Starring Matt Berry Is Here To Refresh The Game With An Ikea Ad
articles.summary: I am not enthusiastic about what feels like an inevitable future wherein games and gaming subscription services are inundated with advertisements. That said, I am excited to reinstall Skyrim so I can play an elaborate Ikea ad.
body: Newly released on Bethesda's Creations site, Kallax Storageborn is a remarkably in-depth Skyrim mod that features the titular Ikea item. But rather than simply adding the Kallax shelving unit as an item you can use to organize your in-game house, the mod turns it into a companion that follows you around, holding an unlimited number of items on your behalf. Oh, and the Kallax is voiced by Matt Berry.

You can get a taste of the mod in the video below, showing off Berry's performance and even a modified version of the opening "You're finally awake" sequence. There are new items to obtain, including the Allenblade, which looks like a giant allen wrench, and the Meatball Helmet.

With the mod installed, there's a new series of quests that kicks off to find the parts to assemble the Kallax, eventually all culminating in a boss fight. To trigger the quest, you'll have to become over-encumbered, which raises the need for a walking, talking shelving unit in the first place.
points: I am not enthusiastic about what feels like an inevitable future wherein games and gaming subscription services are inundated with advertisements.
That said, I am excited to reinstall Skyrim so I can play an elaborate Ikea ad.

articles.title: Liam Neeson's Non-Stop Action Thriller Has One Crazy Twist — It's Director
articles.summary: The Mongoose stars Neeson as Ryan "Fang" Flanagan, a military veteran who gets caught up in a high-speed, cross-country chase after inadvertently stealing an expensive, high-tech car.
body: Mark Vanselow has been working as Liam Neeson's stuntman for over 20 years and at least as many movies, dating all the way back to an uncredited role in the 2000 film Gun Shy. He's helped Neeson look like a tough-as-nails badass in the Taken movies, the Ice Road films, The Commuter, and Cold Pursuit, to name just a few. But for Neeson's latest, Vanselow is taking on his biggest challenge yet: directing.
For Polygon's Fall Preview, we checked in with Vanselow to discuss navigating the stuntman-to-director pipeline, his approach to the action in The Mongoose, and the deeper meaning behind the movie.

"In the stunt world you kind of move up the ladder to stunt coordinating and then second unit directing, where you're directing a lot of the action," Vanselow says. "I've been doing that for a number of years. And in the position of stunt coordinator or stunt performer, I've worked with some amazing directors throughout my career. So it was like a constant university every day."
His opportunity to direct finally came with The Mongoose, thanks to the support of producers Bart Rosenblatt and Al Corley. Of course, it helped that the star of the film had his back, too.
points: The Mongoose stars Neeson as Ryan "Fang" Flanagan, a military veteran who gets caught up in a high-speed, cross-country chase after inadvertently stealing an expensive, high-tech car.

articles.summary: Following the big Steam leak that revealed achievement lists and more for upcoming games, Microsoft has officially released the list of Achievements for Gears of War: E-Day, and there is a Shrek/Smash Mouth-inspired one among them.
body: Players can unlock an achievement called "HEY NOW, YOU'RE AN ALL STAR..." by accumulating 25,000 kills in the Versus multiplayer mode. This Achievement provides 25 Gamerscore.

The most difficult Achievement to unlock appears to be "Dead Serious," which requires players to 100% the campaign on the highest difficulty, Insane, reach 25,000 kills in Versus, achieve max player level, and max out four classes. Players who do that will be rewarded with 85 Gamerscore, which is the most for any single Achievement in the game.

It is a big year for both Xbox and Shrek, as both celebrate their 25th anniversaries this year. The original Shrek movie was re-released in theaters this past summer, and Shrek himself showed up in various video games. As for Xbox, the biggest news event for the 25th anniversary has been Microsoft's decision to lay off thousands of people, close development studios, and cancel games.

articles.title: PlayStation tried to cancel Hideo Kojima's Physint, now Xbox is publishing it
articles.summary: Physint has been hyped as Kojima Productions' return to "tactical espionage action" or, in other words, Hideo Kojima's return to making stealth action games in the style of Metal Gear Solid.
body: "In mid-June of this year, we unexpectedly received notice from PlayStation Studios that they would cancel the Physint project," Hideo Kojima wrote on X.

"Physint is an important project both to me personally and to Kojima Productions. Determined to keep the project alive, we have spent the last three months searching tirelessly for a new partner. In the course of seeking advice and pursuing negotiations with people across many fields, we found in Xbox a partner with whom we share a common vision for the future, and we have decided to team up with them once again.
"Please rest assured that development of Physint, our genre-defining action-espionage title, is ongoing and will continue moving forward."
In an exceedingly rare turn of events, Sony has even released its own statement, though it's unlikely to paper over the fact that the company tried to cancel a Hideo Kojima game.
points: Physint has been hyped as Kojima Productions' return to "tactical espionage action" or, in other words, Hideo Kojima's return to making stealth action games in the style of Metal Gear Solid.

articles.title: The next game by the creators of Steins;Gate is an entirely vibe-coded FPS slopfest
articles.summary: Juggernaut is a forthcoming free-to-play boomer shooter clearly styled after Wolfenstein engine FPSes of yore. It's about shooting huge waves of zombies in flat, pixellated arenas.
body: It's the work of Mages Inc, a Japanese studio best known for the Steins;Gate series of visual novels; it has also worked on recent iterations of the Corpse Party series. Mages Inc generally specialises in visual novels, though it has released at least one Xbox 360 action game that was never released outside of Japan.

In other words, this FPS is entirely vibe-coded, and its assets are overwhelmingly the work of generative AI. The Juggernaut Asset Maker, which will cost money, carries a similar disclosure: "The source code for this application was generated using generative AI".

Mages Inc isn't the best known studio in the world, but it's been around for over 20 years and has issued a handful of games that most enthusiasts would have heard of. Steins;Gate has nearly 6,000 "overwhelmingly positive" reviews on Steam; the recent Steins;Gate Re:Boot, which was released on August 20, already has nearly 600 "very positive" reviews.

So it's surprising how heavily they're leaning into generative AI with Juggernaut. Some Steam users have taken to the Juggernaut discussions board to air their grievances: "If you don't care enough to make a game why should I care enough to buy it?" one user asks.
points: Juggernaut is a forthcoming free-to-play boomer shooter clearly styled after Wolfenstein engine FPSes of yore.

points: Hot off the heels of The Legend of Zelda 40th Anniversary Direct that revealed a ton of new gameplay and information for the Ocarina of Time Remake, Nintendo brings us another Nintendo Direct with…
Among the reveals were a brand new Metroid game with Metroid Ravenous, and a brand new open sandbox Kirby game with Kirby and the World Beyond.
There were also tons of third party games announced and being ported to the Nintendo Switch 2.
